key_insight: SpatialEdit-Bench provides the first comprehensive benchmark that jointly measures perceptual plausibility and geometric fidelity for fine-grained image spatial editing, using viewpoint reconstruction and framing analysis to quantify how well edits preserve realistic appearance and correct geometry.
problem_solved: Current image-editing evaluations ignore or inadequately measure geometry—there was no standardized suite for assessing fine-grained, geometry-driven spatial edits (object layout and camera viewpoint changes). This benchmark fills that gap.
method: Curate SpatialEdit-Bench: a dataset of spatial-editing tasks with ground-truth viewpoints, framing annotations, and edited target images.
Define joint evaluation metrics: perceptual plausibility (e.g., realism / perceptual similarity) combined with geometric fidelity via viewpoint reconstruction and framing analysis.
Provide a standardized evaluation protocol and baseline model assessments to reveal trade-offs between visual realism and geometric accuracy.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare spatial-editing models along both visual and geometric axes, accelerating improvements for applications like AR, scene synthesis, and robotics that require precise layout and viewpoint control.
visual_elements: Before/after edit examples with overlaid camera poses and object bounding/framing to show spatial change
Scatter plot comparing methods on perceptual plausibility vs. geometric fidelity (trade-off visualization)
Benchmark pipeline diagram: dataset → metrics (perceptual + geometric) → evaluation protocol → baselines
Heatmap or icon-based framing analysis showing where edits violate expected camera framing or object placement
paper_title: SpatialEdit: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Image Spatial Editing
paper_authors: Yicheng Xiao, Wenhu Zhang, Lin Song, Yukang Chen, Wenbo Li
